title: EO documentation: reconcile ordinary dispatch and nonblocking-send contracts
outcome: The current docs match the code after the per-turn gating removal: no page describes a gated admission or recovery route, verification_bind credit, or a removed client field as current behaviour, and the execution-observability page states the one remaining synchronous Engram read on the send path accurately.
acceptance: docs/architecture.md endpoint table (about line 450) describes ordinary dispatch for an omitted origin and conservative retention of unknown deliveries for queue/resume, with no gated admission or gated recovery.

docs/features/host-architecture.md no longer presents verification_bind binding batch members (about lines 373 and 990) or engramBootRecoveryPending (about line 1125) as current; either the paragraphs are updated or the historical disclaimer covers them.

docs/features/execution-observability.md (about line 67) either qualifies 'Sends, queue drains, Resume and mailbox wakes do not wait for Engram' for the context-nudge read (prepare_engram_context_nudge_off_lock, up to about 7 s), or that read is taken off the send path in a separate change.

The records-from-earlier-builds text states that retained observation envelopes whose stored request carries routing_token settle as LocalFailure runtime_observation_invalid_retained_image without being sent, and the deliberate removal of the Claude gate write guard is recorded.

completion.summary:
No doc change was needed: all four criteria were already met on master 2a873f3b by earlier landings, as recorded with exact line quotes in note 112653ca.
- architecture.md endpoint table: ordinary dispatch and conservative retention.
- host-architecture.md: no current verification_bind or engramBootRecoveryPending.
- execution-observability.md: sends never wait on an Engram context read. The read left the send path in 5e1fd9a4.
- engram-host-adapter.md: routing_token LocalFailure, and the gate write guard's removal is recorded.
The independent evaluation passed all four.
